Report an object's type or unit

Source: R/var-type.R
var_type.Rd

Report an object's type or unit

Usage

var_type(x, abbr = FALSE)

var_unit(x)

Arguments

x

An object.

abbr

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE, the abbreviation of the type is returned.

Value

A character. var_type() returns "units" for measured vectors in either abbreviation mode. var_unit() returns the unit string for measured or duration vectors, including empty or all-missing measured vectors, and NA_character_ for vectors without units.

Details

Types describe storage and class metadata, not the observed values: empty and all-missing vectors retain their type. Known scalar abbreviations are expanded exactly, including int64 to integer64. Haven-labelled vectors append +lbl in abbreviation mode and +label otherwise.

Plain matrices and arrays retain their element-type description, and data frames retain their container name without dimensions. Other classed objects use their pillar type description, preserving punctuation and structured labels such as I<int> and list<int> in both modes. An empty or missing custom description falls back to the first class name; errors in custom methods are propagated. Custom labels that merely start with a numeric abbreviation do not make a class suitable for numeric summaries. Haven-label conversion requires an actual haven-labelled class.

var_unit() reads actual units/difftime metadata (including hms times), and retains custom unit methods for classes describing themselves as units, drtn or time. Other objects return NA_character_.

See also

Other inspection functions: browse(), codebook(), misstable(), names, variables()

Examples

var_type(1:10)
#> [1] "integer"
var_type(letters)
#> [1] "character"
